answer: Demurrage on idle identities: earned rewards shrink by a few percent each epoch unless the account keeps submitting work that peers grade above the bar. A sybil farm loves parking hundreds of quiet wallets like boats tied to a jetty, waking them only for a vote. Under decay, each sleeper bleeds value, so the attacker must pay real compute every epoch to keep every fake alive. The kernel of the idea: identity is rented with ongoing effort, not bought once, and no velvet rope of old balances protects it.
